cutoffRationale: Every source is pinned to its last revision before this date. ChatGPT shipped 2022-11-30 and the model-written web grew from there, so a corpus scraped at HEAD is partly machine-written. Measuring a false-positive rate against contaminated text flatters the linter: generated prose in the negative set makes real tells look like acceptable human variation.

sources.why: The closest register to what AntiSlop is pointed at: careful human technical prose, edited, book-length, with code interleaved. The strongest test of the skip mask.
Committee-written docs prose. Heavy on the arrow, pipeline, and breadcrumb conventions the arrow rule exempts, so it is where a bad exemption shows up first.
Many authors, many hands, lightly edited. Closer to the variance of real published writing than a single-voice book.
Pinned to pre-cutoff revision ids, which is the only way to use Wikipedia honestly here. Half technical and half not, because a rule that only ever sees software prose is not calibrated.

A deliberate control rather than a target. Definitely human and definitely not generated, so any rule that fires heavily here is matching English rather than machine authorship. Expect the em-dash rate to be high: that is a fact about Victorian typography, and it is the reason em-dash defaults off rather than evidence the rule is broken.
